final_text:
I checked the 10 organisms listed for spike_P0 in `truth/spike_manifest.tsv` against the species-level (rank S) rows in `data/spike_P0.report.gz`. An organism counts as detected if its clade read count is at least 10. Five organisms passed and five did not.

| Organism (manifest) | Spiked pairs | Clade reads (S) | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pseudomonas aeruginosa | 40,000 | 811 | detected |
| Escherichia coli | 4,000 | 72 | detected |
| Salmonella enterica | 400 | 4 | missed |
| Lactobacillus fermentum (reported as Limosilactobacillus fermentum) | 40 | 26 | detected |
| Enterococcus faecalis | 40,000 | 6,457 | detected |
| Staphylococcus aureus | 4,000 | 54 | detected |
| Listeria monocytogenes | 400 | not in report | missed |
| Bacillus subtilis | 40 | 2 | missed |
| Saccharomyces cerevisiae | 40,000 | not in report | missed |
| Cryptococcus neoformans | 4,000 | not in report | missed |

Three organisms have no species-level row in the report, so I counted them as 0 reads. The report can't tell us whether that's because Kraken2 found nothing or because those species (two of them yeasts) aren't in the database.

Recovered read counts are far below the number of pairs added. For example, Saccharomyces had 40,000 pairs added and none were found, while Lactobacillus fermentum had only 40 added and 26 were found.
